run.question:
EU prod is having a checkout incident — 500s on POST /api/checkout. Investigate
using the app-267-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The app-267-prod-logs index (only index matching app-267-*, green, 4 documents total) holds exactly four documents in the authorized window, all stamped cluster=acme-prod-eu-west-1, environment=prod, region=eu-west-1. They record: checkout-service ERROR 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (adyen-eu)' at 2026-11-22T08:11:16Z; payment-service ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms' at the same second 08:11:16Z; checkout-service ERROR 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 36%)' at 09:11:16Z; and payment-service WARN 'adyen-eu degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=620' at 09:41:16Z. The deepest cause the evidence names is the upstream payment provider adyen-eu: the payment-service error text attributes the 30 s timeout to adyen-eu /v68/payments, and the later WARN records adyen-eu in degraded mode. checkout-service is affected by its own error line, and payment-service by its own upstream-timeout error line. Cluster-side checks found no app-267 namespace or objects; the cluster's own otel-demo services are differently named (component labels checkout and payment, not checkout-service and payment-service) and were healthy during the window: the payment pod logged 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' pairs from 08:05:46 to 08:14:35 including 08:11:30, and checkout logged 'payment went through' continuously from 08:23 to 10:10 with no error-matching lines. All flagd fault flags (incl. paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable) are at defaultVariant off, and the only events in the window concern an unrelated app-223 sqlserver pod start plus three FailedToCreateEndpoint warnings for app-219/mariadb, app-95/orca and app-162/signup-service. A cluster-wide container restart at 08:04:13Z hit every pod including kube-system at one instant and was followed by successful charges, so it is not tied to this cause. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable for the whole run, so there is no error-rate, latency or trace corroboration, and the index records no HTTP status codes, so the '500' status and the full incident span are not directly observed.

claims.text: The index app-267-prod-logs is the only index matching app-267-* (health green, docs.count 4) and holds exactly 4 documents inside the authorized window, all with cluster=acme-prod-eu-west-1, environment=prod, region=eu-west-1.
checkout-service logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-22T08:11:16Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (adyen-eu)'.
payment-service logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-22T08:11:16Z: 'Upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms'.
checkout-service logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-22T09:11:16Z: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 36%)'.
payment-service logged level=WARN at 2026-11-22T09:41:16Z: 'adyen-eu degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=620'.

The log index contains no HTTP status field (mapped fields are cluster, environment, level, message, region, service, timestamp), so the specific 500 status code and the number of failed POST /api/checkout requests are not recorded in this evidence.

No namespace or workload for app-267 exists in cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1; the namespaces present are app-223, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo, so checkout-service and payment-service have no pod status, events or container logs readable here.

The cluster's otel-demo pods are labeled app.kubernetes.io/component=checkout and app.kubernetes.io/component=payment, and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME is derived from that label, so the cluster's service identities are 'checkout' and 'payment' — not the 'checkout-service' and 'payment-service' recorded in the log index.

The cluster's otel-demo payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d logged 'Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.' for each charge from 2026-11-22T08:05:46Z through 08:14:35Z, including a completed transaction at 08:11:30Z (transactionId f3350aec-462c-4de1-9c45-27a94d4969e2), i.e. it was serving charges successfully during the window in which payment-service's adyen-eu timeout was logged.

The cluster's otel-demo checkout pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logged 'payment went through (transaction_id: …)' plus 'order confirmation email sent' continuously from 08:23:54Z to 10:10:21Z, and an error-term log search over 07:30–09:20Z matched no failure lines (only info lines containing 'payment went through').

Both otel-demo deployments are healthy: checkout (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout) and payment (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment) each report spec.replicas 1, readyReplicas 1, updatedReplicas 1 with conditions Available=True (MinimumReplicasAvailable) and Progressing=True (NewReplicaSetAvailable), and the pods are Running/ready with restartCount 2.

All otel-demo and kube-system containers show a previous instance terminated with finishedAt 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z (exitCode 255, reason Unknown, startedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:48Z), i.e. a cluster-wide restart of every workload including control-plane pods at one instant, not a checkout- or payment-specific change.

In the otel-demo flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) every fault flag is off: paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad all have defaultVariant 'off'.

The only events inside the window are 9 records: an unrelated app-223 sqlserver pod rollout (Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Deployment ScalingReplicaSet on sqlserver) and three Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint events for app-219/mariadb, app-95/orca and app-162/signup-service; none concerns checkout, payment or adyen.

An error-term log search of the cluster's payment pod over 07:00–10:00Z returned only one line, a Node MetadataLookupWarning at 2026-11-22T08:04:24Z ('Invalid response from metadata service: incorrect Metadata-Flavor header'), and no payment/adyen/retry/circuit errors.

The adyen-eu dependency is external to the observed cluster: the otel-demo service list has no adyen/adyen-eu service (services are ad, alertmanager, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, jaeger-*, kube-state-metrics, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, product-catalog, prometheus, prometheus-readonly-proxy, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart), and payment's deployment env carries no provider endpoint (only PAYMENT_PORT, FLAGD_HOST, FLAGD_PORT and OTEL_* variables).

The checkout-service circuit breaker recorded at 09:11:16Z (failure rate 36%) is a secondary mechanism that makes later POST /api/checkout calls fail fast while the payment-service→adyen-eu path stays degraded; the index does not show how many requests it rejected or when it closed.

The adyen-eu retry backlog (retry queue depth=620 at 09:41:16Z) may have amplified payment-service latency and kept retries in flight after the initial 08:11:16Z timeout, but no metric series (retry queue depth, latency, error rate) was retrievable to confirm duration or scale.

Injected payment failure in the observed cluster (flagd paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable) is not the cause: both flags have defaultVariant off and the cluster's own payment pod kept completing charges through the error window.

The cluster-wide container restart at 08:04:13Z is not the cause of the checkout 500s: it terminated container instances of every pod at the same instant (including kube-system/control-plane) rather than applying a checkout- or payment-specific change, and the cluster's payment pod completed charges normally from 08:05:46Z onward and at 08:11:30Z, during the logged adyen-eu timeout.

Against treating the observed cluster's checkout/payment as the affected entities: their identities differ (component labels checkout/payment vs. checkout-service/payment-service in the index), the checkout pod logged only successful payments (08:23:54Z–10:10:21Z) with no error lines in 07:30–09:20Z, the payment pod logged only completed transactions in 08:05–08:15Z, and the only events in the window concern unrelated app-223 sqlserver objects and other apps' endpoint warnings.

Get the adyen-eu provider timeline (status-page incident start/end and the /v68/payments failure window) for 2026-11-22 08:00–10:00Z to confirm the degradation period and to decide whether checkout-service should shorten its 30 s provider timeout or tune its circuit-breaker threshold.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for the whole run: get_metric_names, get_label_values and execute_prometheus_instant_query each returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (including a query of kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{namespace="otel-demo",deployment=~"payment|checkout"}), so no error-rate or latency series (e.g. traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name,span_name,status_code}, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, app_payment_transactions_total) could be read and no latency baseline exists.

Jaeger was unreachable for the whole run: traces_search (checkout and payment) and traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level confirmation of the checkout-service→payment-service→adyen-eu call edge, its error status or its durations.

The log index holds only 4 documents in the authorized window, so it cannot establish the full count of failed POST /api/checkout requests, the incident start/end, or recovery; it also carries no HTTP status field, so the 500 status itself is unverified.

checkout-service and payment-service have no Kubernetes objects in cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1 (no app-267 namespace), so their pod status, container restart reasons, events and application logs could not be examined.

A cluster-wide configmap search for 'adyen' returned no matching configmap, so where adyen-eu is configured/allow-listed could not be verified; no adyen service, host or endpoint is visible in the cluster, and secrets cannot be read.

There was no observation of the adyen-eu degradation itself (only the in-app error and status-page WARN), and the change-history integration is not available in this Run, so when the provider degraded or recovered and what changed on adyen-eu is unknown.
Circuit-breaker behaviour in checkout-service (whether it stayed open, how many requests it rejected, when it closed) is not observable from the four log lines.
next_steps: Obtain the adyen-eu status-page incident timeline for 2026-11-22 08:00–10:00Z and correlate it with the 08:11:16Z /v68/payments timeout and 09:41:16Z degraded-mode acknowledgement.

Re-run the Prometheus and Jaeger checks when those sources are reachable to quantify checkout-service 5xx rate, payment-service provider-call latency and any completed/errored spans around 08:11Z and 09:11Z.
Locate the actual checkout-service/payment-service workload (namespace/host of app-267) and read its pod status, events and logs, including previous container instances.

Review checkout-service timeout, retry/backoff and circuit-breaker settings together with payment-service retry-queue handling, since a 30 s provider timeout plus a 620-deep retry queue can extend impact beyond the provider outage.
